title: Refund Inbox
intro: Ten messages promising money back. One minute.
Swipe left if it is a scam, right if it is safe. Or tap the buttons.
Some refunds are real. Do not turn away your own money.

cards.text: You are eligible for a tax refund of $412.80. Claim it now: civic-refund.claims/start
cards.why: Tax offices do not text or email to ask you to claim a refund through a link.

cards.text: We have refunded £18.00 for your returned item to your original payment method. Nothing else to do.
cards.why: You returned the item, the money goes back to where it came from, and it asks for nothing.

cards.text: You overpaid your bill by $96.20. Enter your bank details to receive it: brightgrid-refund.net
cards.why: A real energy company does not ask you for bank details by text to refund an overpayment.

cards.text: Your parcel was delayed. Claim your £5 refund: parcelo-compensation.co/claim
cards.why: A refund you never asked for, through a link, from an address that is not the courier's.

cards.text: Your refund of £12.50 from Gadgetz Direct has arrived in your account.
cards.why: It tells you something that already happened, and asks for nothing.

cards.text: Your subscription renews for $349. Not you? Call 0800 555 0188 now for a refund.
cards.why: A big surprise charge and a phone number to call is how support scams begin. Check the number on your own account.

cards.text: Final notice: you will be arrested unless you confirm your refund details at once.
cards.why: Government offices do not threaten arrest over a refund.

cards.text: Your overpayment of £4.30 has been credited to your next bill. No action needed.
cards.why: It happens inside your account and asks for nothing.

cards.text: You are owed compensation for a data breach. Send a small processing fee to receive £3,000.
cards.why: Real refunds never ask you to pay a fee first.

cards.text: Sent you the €15 for the cinema tickets, check your account 🎬
cards.why: A friend you know. If you want to be sure, check your own account, not a link.

golden_rule: Real refunds go back to where the money came from. If you must click, pay a fee or give bank details to get money, it is a scam.

quick_check.q: A text says you overpaid and asks for your bank details to send a refund. What do you do?

options.text: Send the details, it is your money
Do not reply. Check your bill or account using contact details you already know
Click the link but only look

quick_check.explain: Real companies refund to where the money came from. They never need your bank details by text.
